reasoning_log_text: The study investigates predictive coding in mouse visual cortex using locomotion and feedback mismatch. For LO (Local Oddball), Activity Suppression is supported by the finding that visual input alone is a poor predictor of activity (Figure 1B), suggesting motor/contextual factors drive responses, which relates to suppression mechanisms. E/I Balance Shift is weakly supported by the finding that motor-related input drives responses in the absence of visual input (Page 5). For GO (Global Oddball), Activity Suppression is supported by the general finding that motor-related input drives activity, similar to LO. Inhibition (GABA) is weakly supported by the general framework of predictive coding mechanisms being discussed, though not directly quantified. VIP-Mediated Disinhibition and Precision Weighting (Gain) are inferred from the discussion of motor/sensory integration but lack direct quantitative evidence. The absence of specific data on SST, PV, Habituation, Synaptic Depression, Selective Sharpening, Alpha/Beta Suppression, and Omission Response results in null scores for those factors.
